Q: X was observed on varying dates across states, mainly in New England. Lincoln's decision to make it a national holiday was a strategic move to foster a sense of "American" identity during the country's most fractured moment.
The proclamation was issued just months after the Union victories at Gettysburg and Vicksburg, entreating all Americans to ask God to "commend to his tender care all those who have become widows, orphans, mourners or sufferers in the lamentable civil strife".
